Based on my search, here's a comprehensive guide on how to type up minutes of a meeting:

## Before the Meeting

1. **Prepare a template** with the basic information already filled in:
   - Organization name
   - Meeting type (e.g., board meeting, team meeting)
   - Date, time, and location (or virtual platform)
   - List of expected attendees

2. **Review the agenda** to understand what will be discussed and create sections accordingly

## During the Meeting

1. **Take concise notes** focusing on:
   - What was done (decisions made)
   - What was agreed to (action items)
   - What was discussed (key points, not word-for-word)

2. **Record essential details:**
   - Start and end times
   - Attendees present and absent
   - Motions made, who made them, and vote outcomes
   - Action items with assigned owners and deadlines

## Standard Format for Typed Minutes

### Header
- Organization/Committee name
- Date and time
- Location
- Meeting called to order by [name] at [time]

### Attendance
- **Present:** List names
- **Absent:** List names
- **Guests:** If applicable

### Approval of Previous Minutes
- Note if previous minutes were approved, with or without corrections

### Agenda Items
For each item, include:
- Topic heading
- Summary of discussion (brief)
- Any decisions made
- Action items (who, what, by when)

### Other Business
- Any additional topics discussed

### Action Items Summary
- Table listing: Task | Assigned to | Due Date

### Next Meeting
- Date, time, location if scheduled

### Adjournment
- Time meeting ended
- Name of person taking minutes

## Key Writing Tips

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Use past tense | Use first person ("I") |
| Be objective and neutral | Include opinions or judgments |
| Use clear, simple language | Write verbatim transcripts |
| Include specific numbers, dates, amounts | Be vague about decisions |
| Use bullet points for readability | Write long paragraphs |

## Final Steps

1. **Review and edit** for clarity, accuracy, and completeness
2. **Circulate for approval** to the meeting chair or secretary
3. **Distribute promptly** (typically within 24-48 hours)
4. **File securely** for future reference and legal compliance

## Sample Template Structure

```
MEETING MINUTES

[Organization Name]
[Committee/Team Name]
Date: [Date]
Time: [Start] – [End]
Location: [Address/Platform]

ATTENDEES
Present: [Names]
Absent: [Names]

1. CALL TO ORDER
[Name] called the meeting to order at [time].

2. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MINUTES
[Result – approved as presented/as amended]

3. AGENDA ITEMS

3.1 [Topic]
Discussion: [Brief summary]
Decision: [If applicable]
Action: [Task] – [Name], due [date]

[Continue for each item...]

4. ACTION ITEMS SUMMARY
| Action Item | Owner | Due Date |
|-------------|-------|----------|
|             |       |          |

5. NEXT MEETING
[Date, time, location]

6. ADJOURNMENT
Meeting adjourned at [time].

Respectfully submitted,
[Name]
[Title]
[Date]
```

Minutes serve as the official record of what occurred and may have legal significance, so accuracy and objectivity are essential.

Sources:
1. https://www.asme.org/career-education/articles/team-building/how-to-take-meeting-minutes
2. https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/how-to-take-meeting-minutes
3. https://www.wildapricot.com/blog/how-to-take-meeting-minutes
4. https://www.betterup.com/blog/how-to-write-meeting-minutes
5. https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/how-to-take-meeting-minutes
